findings.passage: In a Zoom conversation recorded in May 2025 and published by [Interview](https://www.interviewmagazine.com/theater/meet-ella-beatty-daughter-of-hollywood-royalty-and-sarah-paulsons-kindred-spirit) that June, Paulson asked whether she had ever thought she shouldn't use her last name. Beatty said no.
findings.problem: The question is broadened. In the Interview transcript Paulson asks, 'When you were at Juilliard, did you ever think, "I shouldn't have my last name?"' Beatty answers 'No', then: 'It really never occurred to me until I started working.' With 'at Juilliard' dropped, 'Beatty said no' reads as a blanket denial, while the next quote says the thought did come once she was working. The quotation is accurate; the framing of the question is not. Claim C75 records the question correctly but its passage drops the qualifier.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence restores the Juilliard frame, e.g. 'Paulson asked whether, at Juilliard, she had ever thought she shouldn't use her last name. Beatty said no.' C75's passage matches the new wording exactly. The quotation that follows is unchanged.

findings.passage: And the one report of nerves with nothing at stake, between performances in 2025, is hard to put down to a first lead.
findings.problem: In Interview (S04) the nerves come mid-run of Sexual Misconduct of the Middle Classes, a two-hander opposite Hugh Jackman (in effect a co-lead), during gaps of 'four or five days between performances'. She ties them to missing the play ('I'm finding being away from the play really hard... I miss it when I'm away from it'). The next performance was still ahead, so 'nothing at stake' is the author's overstatement. 'Hard to put down to a first lead' also leans on treating Monster as her first lead, though this run was itself a lead stage role. The datum is real and is one of the two observations the editor used to answer enneagram-01. The earlier paragraph gives the context correctly ('she missed the play'), so this is a wording repair, not a missing source.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence says only what S04 supports, e.g. 'the one report of nerves away from any opening, audition or first night, on days off in the middle of a 2025 run', and drops 'nothing at stake'. Either it drops the 'first lead' contrast or it says it was mid-run rather than opening nerves. C57's passage and inference match. The Six case still marks the datum as her own account.

findings.passage: Her accounts of pressure point outward, to "so many people to please" and not leaving people "in the lurch."
findings.problem: The body is 2,952 words by checkDraft, about 18% over the roughly 2,500-word open-case target, and the weighing section re-quotes material the reader has just met. 'So many people to please' appears three times in the body, and 'Exceptionally poised' and 'make me separate' twice each. It is not padding, and every addition answered a jury finding. But the recaps slow the weighing section slightly. This is not a release gate.
findings.acceptance_test: Optional, at the next refresh: the weighing section points back to evidence already quoted instead of re-quoting it, bringing the body nearer 2,500 words. No sourced counterevidence, alternative-type evidence or settle signal is removed.
